tool_args.rationale: The observed response is monotone and concave, but u_now and s_grad rise together across all five rows. A high-s_grad regime probe can help distinguish gradient-sink behavior from alternative smooth responses before fitting.

considered_alternatives.option: Author a hydraulic basin siphon model now
considered_alternatives.rejected_reason: The five observations vary u_now and s_grad together, so their separate effects and any branch contribution are not identifiable.

considered_alternatives.option: Author a Cobb-Douglas or other smooth saturating model now
considered_alternatives.rejected_reason: The same input confounding prevents distinguishing these model families from the hydraulic candidate at the current conditions.
A targeted high-s_grad observation is more directly useful for separating gradient dependence from u_now response.
It is not relevant to resolving the current identifiability ambiguity.
